literal: That year, Prince You of Qi, Prince Ling of Rencheng, Prince Xiu of Langye, and Prince Gai of Xindu died.
idiomatic: That year Princes You, Ling, Xiu, and Gai died.

literal: In the eighth year’s ninth month, a star broomed at the Southern Dipper, several tens of rods long, extinguished after many days.
idiomatic: Year eight, September: a vast broom star on the Dipper lasted many days.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Dipper governs noble rank and stipend; the state will have great grief."
idiomatic: The Dipper ties to offices and stipends; the realm faces deep sorrow.

literal: One gloss says: "When it brooms the Dipper, the king will be ill, under Heaven governance will change, and great disorder and arms will arise."
idiomatic: A variant adds royal illness, political overturn, and massive war.

literal: In the first Taixi year’s fourth month, a guest star was in the Purple Palace.
idiomatic: Taixi one, April: a guest star shone in the Purple Palace.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
idiomatic: War and death follow.

literal: Near the end of Taikang, Emperor Wu indulged feasts and outings and had many illnesses.
idiomatic: Late Taikang saw Emperor Wu lost in revels and sickness.

literal: In that month, day Jiyou, the emperor died.
idiomatic: That month, jiyou: the emperor died.

literal: In the first Yongping year, Empress Jia executed Yang Jun and his partisans, all exterminating three clans; Empress Dowager Yang was also murdered.
idiomatic: Yongping one: Empress Jia wiped out Yang Jun’s faction to the third degree and killed Empress Dowager Yang.

literal: She also executed Prince Liang of Runan, Grand Guardian Wei Guan, and Prince Wei of Chu—responses to royal-house arms and mourning.
idiomatic: She also killed Princes Liang and Wei and Grand Guardian Wei Guan—royal bloodletting matching the omens.

literal: In Emperor Hui’s fifth Yuankang year, fourth month, there was a star brooming in the Strider, reaching the Coachman and Supreme Palace Enclosure, passing the Three Steps and Great Tomb.
idiomatic: Yuankang five, April: a broom star ran from Kui through Xuanyuan and the enclosure across Three Steps and Great Tomb.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Strider is Lu and also armory troops; the Coachman is the rear palace; the Supreme Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven’s court; the Three Steps are the three ministers; the Great Tomb has piled corpses and death-mourning affairs."
idiomatic: Kui marks Lu and arsenals; Xuanyuan the harem; the enclosure the court; Three Steps the ministers; Great Tomb mass death.

literal: Afterward the armory burned and the western Qiang rebelled.
idiomatic: Then the arsenal caught fire and western Qiang rose.

literal: After five years, Minister of Works Zhang Hua met disaster; Empress Jia was deposed and died; Duke Lu Jia Mi was executed.
idiomatic: Five years on: Zhang Hua perished, Empress Jia fell, and Jia Mi died.

literal: The next year, Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne.
idiomatic: Next year Prince Zhao Lun seized the throne.

literal: Thereupon the three princes raised arms against Lun; soldiers who died in battle exceeded one hundred thousand.
idiomatic: Three princes marched on Lun and left a hundred thousand dead.

literal: In the first Yongkang year’s third month, an uncanny star appeared in the south.
idiomatic: Yongkang one, March: a freak southern star.

literal: The prognostication states: "When an uncanny star appears, under Heaven great arms will arise."
idiomatic: Uncanny stars herald realm-wide war.

literal: That month Empress Jia killed the heir; Prince Zhao Lun soon deposed and killed the empress, beheaded Minister of Works Zhang Hua, and also deposed the emperor and set himself up.
idiomatic: That month Empress Jia murdered the crown prince; Lun then killed her and Zhang Hua, deposed the emperor, and seized power.

literal: Thereupon the three princes all rose, passing the supreme mandate in turn.
idiomatic: Three princes rose in rotation, each holding the reins.

literal: That twelfth month, a comet issued west of the Oxherd, pointing at the Celestial Market.
idiomatic: That December a comet sprang west of the Oxherd toward the Celestial Market.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Ox is the beginning of the seven regulators; when a comet issues from it, it is an image of changing era-name and altering reign-title."
idiomatic: The Ox opens the seven celestial powers; a comet there means new era names.

literal: The Celestial Market is also called the Celestial Treasury and also called the Son of Heaven’s banner; the emperor’s seat lies within it.
idiomatic: The Market is heaven’s treasury, the royal banner, with the throne inside.

literal: The next year, Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne, changed the era-name, and soon was destroyed by a great army.
idiomatic: Next year Lun seized power, changed the era, then fell to a great host.

literal: In the second year’s fourth month, a comet appeared in Qi’s division.
idiomatic: Year two, April: a comet in Qi’s sector.

literal: The prognostication states: "Qi will have arms and mourning."
idiomatic: Qi faces war and death.

literal: At the time Prince of Qi, Jiong, raised troops to campaign against Prince Zhao Lun.
idiomatic: Prince Jiong of Qi marched against Zhao Lun.

literal: When Lun was destroyed, Jiong held troops and did not attend court, monopolizing power, dissolute and extravagant.
idiomatic: After Lun fell, Jiong kept armies private, skipped court, and ruled licentiously.

literal: The next year, he was executed.
idiomatic: The following year Jiong was executed.

literal: In the first Tai’an year’s fourth month, a comet was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Tai’an one, April: a daylight comet.

literal: In the second year’s third month, a comet appeared in the east, pointing at the Three Steps.
idiomatic: Year two, March: an eastern comet aimed at the Three Steps.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is an image of arms and mourning."
idiomatic: War and mourning are imaged.

literal: The Three Steps are the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: Three Steps mark the three dukes.

literal: In the third year’s first month, Prince of the Eastern Sea, Yue, seized Grand Commandant and Prince of Changsha, Yi, and Zhang Fang also killed him.
idiomatic: Year three, first month: Sima Yue arrested Sima Yi; Zhang Fang then killed him.

literal: In the first Yongxing year’s fifth month, a guest star guarded the Net.
idiomatic: Yongxing one, May: a guest star stationed at the Net.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Son of Heaven will cut off heirs."
idiomatic: The imperial line risks extinction.

literal: One gloss says: "Great ministers will be executed."
idiomatic: A variant cites ministerial executions.

literal: At the time the various princes held troops; afterward Emperor Hui lost the thread of rule and ultimately had no successor.
idiomatic: Princely armies ruled; Hui never secured an heir.

literal: In the second year’s eighth month, there was a star brooming in the Hairy Head and Net.
idiomatic: Year two, August: a broom through Pleiades and Net.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
idiomatic: War and death again.

literal: The Hairy Head and Net are also Zhao and Wei’s field allotment.
idiomatic: Pleiades-Net map to Zhao-Wei.

literal: On day Dingchou in the tenth month, there was a star brooming at the Northern Dipper.
idiomatic: October, dingchou: a broom on the Dipper.

literal: The prognostication states: "The pearl pivots change hands; the Son of Heaven flees."
idiomatic: The Dipper’s mandate shifts; the emperor runs.

literal: It also says: "A strong state will raise arms; feudal lords will contend for power."
idiomatic: Another line warns of hegemons and baronial strife.

literal: Afterward the various princes crossed arms; each had a response.
idiomatic: Princes then tore at one another, each omen fulfilled.

literal: The next year, Emperor Hui died.
idiomatic: Next year Emperor Hui died.

literal: In Emperor Cheng’s fourth Xianhe year, seventh month, there was a star brooming in the northwest, transgressing the Dipper, extinguished after twenty-three days.
idiomatic: Xianhe four, July: a northwestern broom crossed the Dipper and died in twenty-three days.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is military turmoil."
idiomatic: Mutiny is portended.

literal: In the twelfth month, Guo Mo killed Inspector of Jiang Province Liu Yin; Inspector of Jing Province Tao Kan campaigned against Mo and beheaded him.
idiomatic: December: Guo Mo slew Liu Yin; Tao Kan took his head.

literal: At the time Shi Le also first assumed a usurped title.
idiomatic: Shi Le too began usurping royal styles.

literal: In the second Xiankang year, first month, day Xinsi, a comet was seen at evening in the west, in the Strider.
idiomatic: Xiankang two, first month, xinsi: an evening comet in the Strider.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
idiomatic: War and mourning.

literal: The Strider is also border troops.
idiomatic: Kui also signals frontier armies.

literal: In the third year’s first month, Shi Jilong usurped the title Celestial King.
idiomatic: Third year, first month: Shi Hu took the Celestial King title.

literal: In the fourth year, Shi Jilong campaigned against Murong Huang and did not overcome him.
idiomatic: Year four: Shi Hu attacked Murong Huang without success.

literal: When he withdrew, Huang pursued and struck him, and again defeated Ma Qiu.
idiomatic: On retreat Murong Huang chased him and broke Ma Qiu too.

literal: At the time Huang declared himself a vassal; it matched border troops.
idiomatic: Murong Huang’s submission matched the border-troop omen.

literal: In the sixth year, second month, day Gengchen, there was a star brooming in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: Year six, February, gengchen: a broom in the Supreme Palace.

literal: In the seventh year’s third month, Empress Du died.
idiomatic: Year seven, March: Empress Du died.

literal: In Emperor Kang’s first Jianyuan year, eleventh month, sixth day, a comet appeared in the Neck, seven feet long, white.
idiomatic: Jianyuan one, eleventh month, sixth day: a seven-foot white comet in the Neck.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Neck is the court; it governs arms and mourning."
idiomatic: The Neck marks the court and its wars and funerals.

literal: In the second year, Emperor Kang died.
idiomatic: Year two: Emperor Kang died.

literal: In Emperor Mu’s fifth Yonghe year, eleventh month, day Yimao, a comet appeared in the Neck.
idiomatic: Yonghe five, November, yimao: a comet in the Neck.

literal: Its ray pointed west, white in color, one rod long.
idiomatic: Its tail aimed west, white, one rod long.

literal: On day Dingchou in the sixth year’s first month, a comet again appeared in the Neck.
idiomatic: Year six, first month, dingchou: another Neck comet.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning, pestilence."
idiomatic: War, mourning, and plague.

literal: In that year’s fifth month, eighth month, Chu Pou’s northern expedition was defeated.
idiomatic: That year’s August: Chu Pou’s northern campaign failed.

literal: In the eleventh month, Ran Min killed Shi Zun and also slaughtered more than one hundred thousand Hu; thereupon the central plain was greatly chaotic.
idiomatic: November: Ran Min slew Shi Zun and massacred a hundred thousand Hu, throwing the heartland into chaos.

literal: In the twelfth month, Chu Pou died.
idiomatic: December: Chu Pou died.

literal: That year, great pestilence.
idiomatic: That year brought a great epidemic.

literal: In the second Shengping year, fifth month, day Dinghai, a comet issued from the Celestial Boat, in the Stomach.
idiomatic: Shengping two, May, dinghai: a comet from Celestial Boat in the Stomach.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning, removing the old and spreading the new."
idiomatic: War, death, and renewal.

literal: Issuing from the Celestial Boat means outer barbarians will invade.
idiomatic: From Celestial Boat marks foreign invasion.

literal: One gloss says: "It will be great flood."
idiomatic: A variant cites catastrophic flood.

literal: In the fourth year’s fifth month, under Heaven there was great flood.
idiomatic: Year four, May: realm-wide flooding.

literal: In the fifth year, Emperor Mu died.
idiomatic: Year five: Emperor Mu died.

literal: In Emperor Ai’s first Xingning year, eighth month, there was a star brooming in the Horn and Neck, entering the Celestial Market.
idiomatic: Xingning one, August: a broom from Horn and Neck into the Celestial Market.

literal: Investigating, the prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
idiomatic: Commentary: war and mourning.

literal: In the third year’s first month, Empress Wang died.
idiomatic: Third year, first month: Empress Wang died.

literal: In the second month, the emperor died.
idiomatic: February: the emperor died.

literal: In the third month, Murong Ke attacked and took Luoyang; Shen Jin and others died in battle.
idiomatic: March: Murong Ke took Luoyang; Shen Jin fell fighting.

literal: In Emperor Fei’s fourth Taihe year of the Haixi reign, second month, a guest star appeared on the Purple Palace’s western wall, lasting until the seventh month before it was extinguished.
idiomatic: Haixi Taihe four, February–July: a guest star on the Purple Palace west wall.

literal: The prognostication states: "When a guest star guards the Purple Palace, ministers will murder the ruler."
idiomatic: A guest star on the Purple Palace marks regicide.

literal: In the sixth year, Huan Wen deposed the emperor as Duke of Haixi.
idiomatic: Year six: Huan Wen demoted the sovereign to Duke of Haixi.

literal: In Emperor Xiaowu’s second Ningkang year, first month, day Dingsi, there was a star brooming in Girl and Emptiness, passing the Root, Neck, Horn, Chariot, Wings, and Zhang.
idiomatic: Ningkang two, first month, dingsi: a broom from Girl-Void across Root, Horn, Chariot, Wings, and Zhang.

literal: By the third month’s day Bingxu, a comet appeared in the Root.
idiomatic: Third month, bingxu: a comet showed in the Root.

literal: On day Dingchou in the ninth month, there was a star brooming in the Celestial Market.
idiomatic: September, dingchou: a broom in the Celestial Market.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
idiomatic: War and mourning.

literal: In the first Taiyuan year’s seventh month, Fu Jian broke Liangzhou and captured Zhang Tianxi.
idiomatic: Taiyuan one, July: Fu Jian conquered Liangzhou and took Zhang Tianxi.

literal: In the eleventh Taiyuan year’s third month, a guest star was in the Southern Dipper, lasting until the sixth month before it sank.
idiomatic: Taiyuan eleven, March–June: a guest star lingered in the Dipper.

literal: The prognostication states: "There will be arms; there will be amnesty."
idiomatic: War and pardon both follow.

literal: Afterward Si, Yong, Yan, and Ji constantly had military service.
idiomatic: Si, Yong, Yan, and Ji then saw endless levies.

literal: In the twelfth year’s first month there was a great amnesty; in the eighth month again a great amnesty.
idiomatic: Year twelve: great pardons in first and eighth months.

literal: In the fifteenth year’s seventh month, day Renshen, there was a star brooming at the Northern River Guard, passing the Supreme Palace Enclosure, Three Steps, and Civilized Glory, entering the Northern Dipper, white in color, more than ten rods long.
idiomatic: Year fifteen, July, renshen: a colossal white broom ran from the Northern River Guard through the enclosure, Three Steps, and Civilized Glory into the Dipper.

literal: On day Wuxu in the eighth month, it entered the Purple Palace and then was extinguished.
idiomatic: August, wuxu: it entered the Purple Palace and vanished.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Northern River Guard is also called the Hu Gate; the Hu will have arms and mourning."
idiomatic: The Northern River Guard is the Hu Gate—steppe war and death.

literal: Sweeping the Supreme Palace Enclosure and entering Purple Tenuity means the king will answer for it.
idiomatic: Brushing the enclosure and Purple Tenuity hits the sovereign.

literal: The Three Steps are the Three Dukes; Civilized Glory is generals and ministers; generals and the Three Dukes will have disaster.
idiomatic: Three Steps are dukes; Civilized Glory is generals—both tiers suffer.

literal: Entering the Northern Dipper means feudal lords will be executed.
idiomatic: Entering the Dipper marks executed lords.

literal: One gloss says: "Sweeping the Northern Dipper means a strong state will raise arms, feudal lords will contend for power, and great men will grieve."
idiomatic: A variant adds hegemonic armies, baronial rivalry, and high lords’ mourning.
